title: COLEP: Certifiably Robust Learning-Reasoning Conformal Prediction via Probabilistic Circuits
authors: Mintong Kang, Nezihe Merve GÃ¼rel, Linyi Li, Bo Li
text:
Deep neural networks (DNNs) have demonstrated impressive achievements in different domains [1,2,3,4,5]. However, as DNNs are increasingly employed in real-world applications, particularly those safety-critical ones such as autonomous driving [6] and medical diagnosis [7], concerns regarding their trustworthiness and reliability have emerged [8,9,10,11,12]. To address these concerns, it is crucial to provide the worst-case certification for the model predictions (i.e., certified robustness) [13,14,15], and develop techniques that enable users to statistically evaluate the uncertainty linked to the model predictions (i.e., conformal prediction) [16,17].

In particular, considering potential adversarial manipulations during test time, where a small perturbation could mislead the models to make incorrect predictions [8,18,19,10,20], different robustness certification approaches have been explored to provide the worst-case prediction guarantees for neural networks. On the other hand, conformal prediction has been studied as an effective tool for generating prediction sets that reflect the prediction uncertainty of a given black-box model, assuming that the data is exchangeable [21,22]. Such prediction uncertainty has provided a probabilistic guarantee in addition to the worst-case certification. However, it is unclear how such uncertainty certification would perform in the worst-case adversarial environments.

Although the worst-case certification for conformal prediction is promising, it is challenging for purely data-driven models to achieve high certified prediction coverage (i.e., worst-case coverage with bounded input perturbations). Recent studies on the learning-reasoning framework, which integrates extrinsic domain knowledge and reasoning capabilities into data-driven models, have demonstrated great success in improving the model worst-case certifications [23,24]. In this paper, we aim to bridge the worst-case robustness certification and uncertainty certification, and explore whether such knowledge-enabled logical reasoning could help improve the certified prediction coverage for conformal prediction. We ask: How to efficiently integrate knowledge and reasoning capabilities into DNNs for conformal prediction? Can we prove that such knowledge and logical reasoning enabled framework would indeed achieve higher certified prediction coverage and accuracy than that of a single DNN?

In this work, we first propose a certifiably robust learning-reasoning conformal prediction framework (COLEP) via probabilistic circuits (PCs). In particular, we train different data-driven DNNs in the “learning" component, whose logical relationships (e.g., a stop sign should be of octagon shape) are encoded in the “reasoning" component, which is constructed with probabilistic circuits [25,26] for logical reasoning as shown in Fig 1. Theoretically, we first derive the certified coverage for COLEP under \ell_{2} bounded perturbations. We also provide certified coverage considering the finite size of the calibration set. We then prove that COLEP achieves higher certified coverage and accuracy than that of a single model as long as the knowledge models have non-trivial utilities. To our best knowledge, this is the first knowledge-enabled learning framework for conformal prediction and with provably higher certified coverage in adversarial settings.

We have conducted extensive experiments on GTSRB, CIFAR-10, and AwA2 datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness and tightness of the certified coverage for COLEP. We show that the certified prediction coverage of COLEP is significantly higher compared with the SOTA baselines, and COLEP has weakened the tradeoff between prediction coverage and prediction set size. We perform a range of ablation studies to show the impacts of different types of knowledge.

Conformal prediction is a statistical tool to construct the prediction set with guaranteed prediction coverage [27,22,28,29,30,17,31], assuming that the data is exchangeable. Several works have explored the scenarios where the exchangeability assumption is violated [31,32,33,34,35]. However, it is unclear how to provide the worst-case certification for such prediction coverage considering adversarial setting. Recently, Gendler et al. [36] provided a certified method for conformal prediction by applying randomized smoothing to certify the non-conformity scores. However, such certified coverage could be loose due to the generic nature of randomized smoothing. We propose COLEP with a sensing-reasoning framework to achieve much stronger certified coverage by leveraging the knowledge-enabled logic reasoning capabilities. We provide a comprehensive literature review on certified robustness and logical reasoning in appendix B.
